messages.subject: statistics on Nei's gene diversity for haploid organism
messages.subject_clean: statistics on Nei's gene diversity for haploid organism
messages.body_plain:
Hello,
this may be a silly question to ask, but I have been struggling to find a way how to statistically compare values of Nei's unbiased gene diversity between two populations. I have performed bootstrapping and confidence intervals for genotypic diversity measures (like evenness, Simpson index etc.) but can't find a way how to do it for genic diversity. Basically, I have two populations with Hexp 0.63 vs Hexp 0.76 and I have to find out whether they are statistically different. Will be grateful for suggestions.

Thanks!
Olga

messages.subject: error in poppr.amova
messages.body_plain:
I am trying to do amova in poppr package, for a data on 16 genotypes and 110 markers coded as 0 and 1. First I imported the data as dataframe and converted it to genind object using genind2df, where I added the population and strata levels to the genind object. However, in this data population and strata has only one level, and both are same. I used the following code.

> ader$pop=as.factor(ader$pop) # I converted pop to factor because pop was in numeric format.
> aderg=df2genind(ader[,4:ncol(ader)],ncode=1,ploidy=2, ind.names = ader[[3]], pop=ader[[2]],strata=ader[2])

 But, when I am trying to run poppr.amova command, the following error is displayed
.

Error in `row.names<-.data.frame`(`*tmp*`, value = value) :
  invalid 'row.names' length

I checked the rownames and number of rows, but couldn't find a problem with them as they are numericals from 1 to 16. And the rownames of strata and genind genotype matrix are also matching. What am I missing? Please help me with this.

messages.subject: Re: [poppr] Variance for Hexp
messages.body_plain:
Just realized that the OP never posted the response, which I though was informative.

This solution "works", but there's also a function in pegas called "H", which you can use like so:

library("pegas")
H(genind2loci(nancycats), variance = TRUE)

The only caveat here is that it only works for diploids.

On Tuesday, April 9, 2019 at 10:17:24 AM UTC+1, Zhian Kamvar wrote:

> Hi Kat,
>
> We didn’t add the variance explicitly in poppr and I’m not exactly sure why, because the calculation seems to be fairly straighforward from Nei and Roychaudhury 1974 (http://www.genetics.org/content/genetics/76/2/379.full.pdf), but does get a bit hairy in Nei 1978 (http://www.genetics.org/content/genetics/89/3/583.full.pdf):
>
> Nevertheless, I think I may have a solution for you from the 1974 pub:
>
> The variance is calculated much as you would expect by taking the square residuals and dividing those by the number of loci minus one. Here’s how I would obtain it with the nancycats data set
> suppressPackageStartupMessages(library('poppr'))
> data(nancycats)
> n <- nLoc(nancycats)
> o <- summary(nancycats)$Hobs                # observed heterozygosity
> e <- locus_table(nancycats)[seq(n), "Hexp"] # expected heterozygosity
> #>
> #> allele = Number of observed alleles
> #> 1-D = Simpson index
> #> Hexp = Nei's 1978 gene diversity
> #> ------------------------------------------
> print(v <- ((o - e)^2)/(n - 1))             # per-locus variance
> #>         fca8        fca23        fca43        fca45        fca77
> #> 0.0049759764 0.0020443113 0.0017313233 0.0003610015 0.0071512483
> #>        fca78        fca90        fca96        fca37
> #> 0.0019382048 0.0035164070 0.0025775979 0.0030448688
> mean(v)                                     # overall variance
> #> [1] 0.003037882
>
> Regarding adding this into poppr: I don’t have the bandwith to add the code myself (which includes testing and documentation), but I would be happy to review a pull request from anyone who feels up to the challenge.
>
> Hope that helps!
>
> Zhian
>
> Created on 2019-04-09 by the reprex package <https://reprex.tidyverse.org> (v0.2.1)

> > On Apr 9, 2019, at 09:18 , Kat <REDACTED> wrote:
> >

> > Hi poppr team,
> > Is there a way to obtain the variance of the Hexp in poppr? Could this be added into the R package?
> > Cheers Kat

messages.subject: Re: [poppr] error in poppr.amova
messages.body_plain:
Hi,

> I am trying to do amova in poppr package, for a data on 16 genotypes and 110 markers coded as 0 and 1

It's possible that poppr is interpreting your "0" alleles as missing data, but I'm not certain. Try substituting all your 0 alleles to 2 and see how that works.

>  But, when I am trying to run poppr.amova command, the following error is displayed

You can use the traceback() function to identify where the error came from. Ultimately, there are several factors that could be going on, but I would need a reproducible example to help.

Best,
Zhian
